sources.title: College Physics 2e, 20.2 Ohm's Law: Resistance and Simple Circuits
sources.support_summary: For an ohmic resistor, current equals applied voltage divided by resistance. Ohm's law is not asserted for every possible material.

sources.publisher: US National Human Genome Research Institute
sources.title: Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA) Fact Sheet
sources.locator: What is DNA made of?; What is the DNA double helix?
sources.support_summary: The bases A and T are adenine and thymine; standard DNA complementary pairing joins A with T and C with G.

sources.title: Introduction to Calendars
sources.support_summary: The day tracks Earth's axial rotation, whereas the year tracks its solar revolution. Gregorian century years are leap years only when divisible by 400; 1900 is not and 2000 is.

sources.title: Chemistry 2e, 14.2 pH and pOH
sources.locator: p-function and hydronium molarity equations near the section opening
sources.support_summary: In the text's ideal concentration treatment, hydronium molarity is 10 raised to minus pH; concentration ratios therefore change by powers of ten.

sources.title: Physics, 14.1 Speed of Sound, Frequency, and Wavelength
sources.locator: The Relationship Between the Speed of Sound and the Frequency and Wavelength of a Sound Wave; equation 14.1
sources.support_summary: Wave speed is frequency times wavelength; a change of medium changes speed and wavelength while the driving frequency remains the same under the stated stationary conditions.

sources.title: College Physics 2e, 9.2 The Second Condition for Equilibrium
sources.support_summary: Torque magnitude equals force times perpendicular lever arm; rotational equilibrium requires opposing torques to balance.

sources.title: Biology 2e, 5.2 Passive Transport
sources.support_summary: When only water can cross, water initially moves toward the side with higher concentration of nonpermeating solute, absent a counterbalancing hydrostatic pressure.

sources.title: Biology 2e, 46.2 Energy Flow through Ecosystems
sources.locator: Learning objectives; Productivity within Trophic Levels
sources.support_summary: Food chains transfer energy across trophic levels with less than complete transfer. The panel's exact 10% at each link is a supplied hypothetical efficiency, not claimed as a universal value from this source.

sources.title: Biology 2e, 12.2 Characteristics and Traits
sources.locator: Phenotypes and Genotypes; Dominant and Recessive Alleles
sources.support_summary: Under complete dominance, a recessive phenotype requires the homozygous recessive genotype; monohybrid Punnett-square probabilities follow allele transmission.

sources.title: University Physics Volume 3, 10.3 Radioactive Decay
sources.support_summary: Each half-life halves remaining nuclei and activity. A quarter of the starting sample activity corresponds to two half-lives; the detector's additive background is supplied in the question.

sources.title: University Physics Volume 2, 2.1 Molecular Model of an Ideal Gas
sources.locator: Ideal Gas Law, equation 2.1 and following fixed-number discussion
sources.support_summary: For a fixed number of ideal-gas molecules, absolute pressure times volume divided by absolute temperature is constant.

sources.title: University Physics Volume 2, 10.2 Resistors in Series and Parallel
sources.locator: Opening series/parallel definitions; series equation 10.2; parallel common-voltage definition
sources.support_summary: Series resistors share current and their resistances add. Parallel branches share potential difference and their currents sum, yielding reciprocal addition of conductances.

sources.publisher: US National Aeronautics and Space Administration
sources.title: Jupiter Facts
sources.support_summary: Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System; its quoted size exceeds the other planets. Changing moon counts on the page are not used.

sources.title: Books That Shaped America: 1800 to 1850
sources.locator: Washington Irving, The Legend of Sleepy Hollow (1820)
sources.support_summary: The entry names Washington Irving as author and identifies the story's first publication in 1820.

sources.title: Bank of Japan Notes and Coins Currently Issued
sources.support_summary: The official notes are denominated in yen. The item asks the monetary unit, not a changing exchange rate or note design.

sources.title: Magna Carta
sources.locator: Opening historical paragraph and following reissue paragraph
sources.support_summary: King John sealed Magna Carta at Runnymede on June 15, 1215; the 1297 exhibit version is a later reissue.

sources.title: The Court
sources.support_summary: The Court identifies the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands, as its seat.

sources.title: World Braille Day
sources.support_summary: The page identifies the six-dot tactile system and its nineteenth-century French inventor Louis Braille.

sources.title: Instruments: Oboe
sources.locator: About; orchestral register and section paragraph
sources.support_summary: The orchestra's guide identifies the oboe as a wooden double-reed instrument in the woodwind section.

sources.title: Historic Sanctuary of Machu Picchu
sources.support_summary: The sanctuary is in the Peruvian Andes/Amazon transition, supporting Peru as the country.

sources.publisher: Internet Engineering Task Force / RFC Editor
sources.title: RFC 8200: Internet Protocol, Version 6 (IPv6) Specification
sources.support_summary: IPv6 expands IP address size from IPv4's 32 bits to 128 bits.

sources.title: Metric (SI) Prefixes

sources.title: The Montreal Protocol
sources.support_summary: The Montreal Protocol targets ozone-depleting chemicals and was signed in 1987, entering into force in 1989.
